Really into this game! I've never played a RTS game before, so I was a little intimidated starting out. But this game has a really thorough tutorial, making the game accessible even to a first-time noob like me. That said, I can see how it would quickly get competitive and difficult! My current goal is to complete as many floors as I can without losing any of my clone soldiers, so I play nice and slow. The mechanics are really well balanced. There are more resources available on more difficult floors to defend. The game can quickly get fast-paced, but the ability to plan your buildings while paused helps to even this out. But you can't sit back and keep the swarm on pause; you need further resources to continue building. The other reviews saying this game keeps you itching to play just one more level are no exaggeration. The premise is compelling, the mechanics are fun! I also love the attention to detail; like how body factories have to be built on coal as a realistic resource. Overall, really blown away and enjoying this game!

Easily 8/10 Mack recommended this in his recent video, and I'm glad I checked it out. RTS, tower defense, rouge-like with a few fun twists. Dig until you run out of fuel. Gather what you can and get back to digging. If you stay in the level too long you will perma-die. While in the level you gain upgrades for the current run that you can craft, and bank points that give you permanent upgrades that can be used on the next run. Reminds me a bit of Infested Planet, Mindustry, or Lumencraft. Definitely worth... the price.

This has potential but is missing some basic quality-of-life features that make it difficult to recommend. No saving, no queuing orders, and no way to tell how many resources you are producing in total. Those are just the things I found in the first couple of hours.

For a while, I enjoyed this game. But there are several inherent game design choices which have changed this into a pure slog. --The swarm fury and awareness mechanics are not bad ideas in and of themselves. Swarm awareness acts acts as a timer which prioritizes pushing instead of turtling on a given map, while swarm fury makes the campaign harder the more enemies you kill. However, combined with other design elements, they became headaches which made the game more annoying to play. --The maps are procedurally generated, which is also a good idea. However, their execution is fairly lacking. Resources are also randomly generated, which means you are at the mercy of whether you have enough of the resource nodes close to your starting point to progress quickly enough to keep awareness and fury from building up too much. The real problem, though, is that there are two basic kinds of maps; tunnel maps which provide lots of chokepoints to anchor the defenses on, and cavern maps which are far more open and harder to defend. Given the resource nodes are quite randomly scattered around, they become a nightmare to defend, especially later in the game. --Finally, more powerful tiers of units and structures are gated behind boss levels which prevent you from progressing. It's notable that these levels are always on tunnel maps, since trying to manage the boss on an open plan would be an utter nightmare. However, the problem is that you only start with a handful of blueprints at a given tier, and the only way to get more is to clear levels of that tier; any blueprints you happen to pick up on earlier stages do nothing, even once you get to subsequent tiers. And you can't just rush through the early levels either because of the need to get the currency which unlocks capabilities of your drill. As such I can't really recommend it in its current state. It needs more time in the oven to make sure the mechanics all mesh well, because they are currently somewhat lacking. EDIT--After putting another 40+ hours in and getting better with the mechanics of the game, my opinion is unchanged. I still have yet to reach the boss of the ice boss, because the structure of the game means if I hit one of the wide open ice cavern levels when the swarm is at 150+% rage, I might as well quit and save myself the trouble. I literally could not build up my defenses enough to survive the last two runs when I hit a stage like that, due to the lack of resources I could reach, and it's not fun to have to play multiple levels just to have a run come to a crashing halt like this without even getting to the ice biome boss. Another thing I noticed is that it's possible to reduce drone cooldowns to 0 once you reach the ice biome, which would be great except that any resources being spent on drones are resources that can't be spent on defenses. Drones get really costly once you reach that area, which kind of defeats the purpose of having them since you almost never need them once you have a proper layer of defenses built up. The achievement stats for the game support what I'm saying; 4% of all players who own this game have reached the lava biome. Granted it's not yet three weeks past release, but for that few players to have gotten past where I'm at (and I've spent nearly 80 hours on the game so far) suggests that the difficulty curve is too high at the moment. One thing that would fix the game for me is to have a setting that allows a player to choose what kind of map they play on for that campaign. Players can take the easier tunnel maps for an overall resource reduction, and the harder cavern maps for a resource bonus, or a random mix as it currently stands.

In not understanding how to start with infantry and its ruining the game for me. The first stage you automatically start with units but then the next round i always don't have units starting. Its essential you start with units to explore, so this really becomes a pain in the ass. Maybe I'm missing something, but there seems to not be a clear explanation. Since the game is new, I cant find a solution on the web. The Forge and upgrading process needs more clarity as well. Until then my rating is 2/10
Great game! just needs a bit more variation(more towers) and maybe challenge stages like going infinite

Poorly written w.r.t. window sizing and configuration. You can't even click the button to fix the screen size if you mess up the sizing - by choosing literally any size but the one it defaults to - because clicking stops working. Also you can't save during a mission so you're stuck either abandoning the entire run or leaving the game running in the background, when you need to do something else. The game itself is pretty fun.
simpler, faster they are billions. It really satisfies the build up secure resources expand itch

I really want to like this game, it has a lot of good things going for it. But it ends up being way too grindy with weird jumps in difficulty (both with missions suddenly getting much easier than the previous one as well as sometimes getting much harder, mostly though there's a huge spike when changing into a new biome/area). In addition, it's much too reliant on rng of crafting and map generation. Add to that how slow and repetitive the game is, doing one iteration/run easily taking several hours, the game just ends up feeling like chore with too many random elements hamstringing your play.
The crafting UI is so hideous and irrational that it totally defeats the positive aspects of the core game. Avoid the frustration and play something else.

This game's form of balance is a gym instructor who runs along-side you. If you speed up, they speed up... If you slow down, they dock you points and you have to run extra hard. The idea of "getting ahead" in this game doesn't exist and it makes the challenge not feel worthwhile. If the game's difficult was standard and you could get ahead by gathering extra materials, or fall behind by playing too aggressively/defensively then that would be fine, but it's always like you are a bit behind. Not fun in my opinion :/

At first, the game comes across as a compelling tower defense like, with an addictive loop... But once you've played that loop for over a dozen hours, and have pretty much zero REAL meta progression to show for it, it becomes clear exactly what you're in for... And that's a long, long, grind. While there is an 'easy' mode, it is at the cost of slower meta progression, so no grind reduction. And without any indication of what resources remain on a level, you will find yourself COMPELLED to clear them all, before fueling, because getting the right blueprint can make or break a run. Put simply. There is a lot to like here, but the difficulty ramp up, between levels, compared to the lack of adequate meta progression, and the PAINFUL user interface, means you're going to struggle-grind for dozens of hours, just to see your first 1000+ yard depth. And you'll be LUCKY if you even see a single tier 2 blueprint. If ever.

TL;DR: Good active tower defense at the price point. This game is mislabeled as a "Tower Defense." What it is, is a Tower OFFENSE. The towers are mostly just there to guard your resource farms, except on boss floors where they cover your back while you push the Big Bad. The gameplay feels very solid IMO. But. [strike]BUT. I have almost unlocked all of the permanent upgrades and STILL struggle on the first floor if I don't rush drill fuel and speedrun the boss floor, since the Swarm Rage just goes up uncapped, Its like the devs didnt WANT me collect crafting resources to use the upgrade system they built in. The little time I've spent in floor 2 was miserable cause all of a sudden my units were all irrelevant in the face of the new enemies, and the new units cost double or more than my old ones. On top of that, starting on floor 2, your starting resources are halved. And oh yeah, ♥♥♥♥ your progress through the individual level, enemies now spawn in rooms you've already cleared, anywhere on the map, in clusters that are getting huge because your swarm rage is high by now. The meta progression just does not keep up. For the $6 sale price I got it at I really shouldn't complain.[/strike]Just wish there was some rebalancing. All that ranting having been said, the pixel graphics look awesome, the music is good, the basic mechanics are sound, it runs great with the recommended specs, never once slowing down even when I once had an entire map clogged with about a million mobs. Edit: The rebalancing happened. I only have a few hours playing with the update but it makes the frustrating parts of the game SIGNIFICANTLY less so. UI is nicer now. I [strike]will probably[/strike] put in another 40 hours with no regrets.

My 2 cents on this - I rate a game on how many hours i play on it - 1 hour per £. The game is £7.49 and i've played almost 38 hours on it. I also enjoy how the dev is active and trying his best to improve the game as it goes along. The game is in early access, and people know the risks of early access. All reviews both positive and negative are good as it helps the developer. Negative reviews before a 1.0 release should be constructive, and after the 1.0 release the reviews should be mostly positive because the bad reviews have helped the dev sort problems out. I love that the dev is active with the small community that plays his game in the discord. Ideas flow and the game develops. It gets better slowly over time. My biggest issue is the burrowers. The fact they can show up randomly without much warning really slows down the progression inside the map. My suggestion to fix this is - have burrowers spawn invisible at the spawn points, and walk towards the drill. Then when they attack the drill, their cloak disappears. They ignore everything that can block a normal mob. The only counter is to have the vision tower the only tower that can detect burrowers and will uncloak them. This makes a redundant building useful. :)

This is a bit of a hidden gem. It plays a bit like a rogue-like version of [b]Creeper World 3: Arc Eternal[/b]. For another comparison; Imagine you were struggling in a game of [b]Red Alert[/b] or [b]Age of Empires 2[/b] and were constantly inching your way forward across the map with your army, fighting through a sea of enemies. As you're doing that, you're constantly building little bases and turrets along the way, fighting for every inch of map you can attain. It plays kind of like that. The game revolves around the supply depot buildings, which when placed, allow you to build more buildings in range of it. You end up dotting trails of these across the map, kind of like in [b]Creeper World[/b]. It only takes one enemy to sneak in and abruptly destroy one of these depots, stopping your power supply chain to all of your turrets so they stop working. Because of this vulnerability, every so often you end up building a little fortress along your supply trails, comprised of some walls & turrets. The initial levels are pretty easy, but that quickly changes by the time you've drilled 1000 meters deep. I was banging my head against a wall for a while when I reached that point. ..atleast until I went onto the games Steam discussion page to get a better understanding of one of the games central mechanics: The swarm meter. The longer that you stay in a level, the more the swarm meter rises. This meter affects the strength and number of the enemies and the meter is always rising as you play -it doesn't reset between levels. This means that if you stay in the early levels for too long, you will reach a point where you have basically no chance of making it further. The swarm meter will be too high and enemies will have outraced you in power, making them unmanageable. This makes your runs in the game a race against time, where you need to play fast and efficiently, frequently pausing the game whenever you need to make a decision or manage a minor crisis. You need to be frugal as opposed to greedy when it comes to spending more time in levels searching for loot. As well as having to deal with the swarm meter, after the first 1000 meters, there's a significant difficulty jump in tier 2. The enemies seem to scale up a lot, meanwhile your equipment is still stuck at tier 1. You need to find and craft the tier 2 equipment. It feels necessary to find this equipment in order to keep up with the swarm. This task is easier said than done, especially with the tier 2 units seeming to have twice as much hp requiring you to place twice as many turrets and units to deal with them. Between levels, you can do a decent bit of customization with what kind of troops and buildings you use, and equip them with different items which you will craft. The crafting system is very simple thankfully, I enjoy this aspect of the game. [b]Deep Among the Swarm[/b] can be oppressively difficult even on normal difficulty (there is an easier difficulty option though). I found it necessary to search the games Steam discussion page at least once to work out what I was doing wrong, but I would still consistently hit a wall where it was unclear to me on how to make progress. I imagine a bit of a search on Youtube would possibly teach me more of where I'm going wrong. Despite my struggles with this game (and even if I was to drop it right now) I have had a blast playing this. It's an easy recommendation, I just wish it had a little more variety in the rogue-like aspect, as runs don't feel wildly different from one another. I want more units/turrets/upgrades/maps/enemy types. I also wish that the game was a little clearer on how to improve and make progress.

Great game, beat in about 17 hours all told, but allows for challenge mode to continue the grind. I died twice during my win (dying = use meta resources to buff, then begin again). This scratches the itch of a slow expansion where you have to snuff out enemy spawners, and secure areas. Its similar to they are billions, except you can actually seal off the spawning locations to the point they are no longer a threat. Every run has a bit of RNG when it comes to what items appear, and theres a quasi timer which persists between missions. The timer is the buff the enemy gets which continually rises, so if you dont clear missions in a timely fashion eventually basic 1 hp enemies would have a million hp/ do a million damage etc. The actuality though is if you're moving fairly quickly your units gain strength faster than the enemy and you can stay far ahead of the curve. Great game, probably underpriced considering the care that went into it.

The gameplay itself is enjoyable, but the way the game is set up isn't, which is why I wouldn't recommend it for anyone who doesn't want to invest 50-100 hours+ into a game like this. The game progresses with digging down. Once you lose you'll have to start all the way up from the top again and you'll get to unlock some meta progression that lets you go a little deeper the next time, or make the rounds a bit faster. The individual gameplay levels take way to long to have this be an enjoyable grind, so it just ends up being frustrating.
fun

It has that nice meta progression feel for a quick RTS where you're mostly just positioning troops to defend or purge an area. Good value for the price. Wouldn't mind more depth to the meta progression and structures though, but overall great value and gameplay.

Just didn't grab me, it has serious problems with the execution. Resources fill so fast that it feels like you need to constantly be pausing to queue research / energy spreaders which is just annoying. There's almost zero depth in the resource economy. Aside from the body factories, you just build mines/energy plants on their respective tiles and move on. It suffers from the roguelite curse where it takes 30-60 minutes of play in a run for the game to become harder than dead easy.
I can't tell if it's a bug or intended, but literally invincible, invisible enemies will teleport to your HQ and instantly kill it. Game is literally unplayable.
Peak, 10/10. The game knows what it wants to be and nails it in every way.
Deep Among the Swarm is a thrilling RTS with tower defense elements that relies on playing quickly as the difficulty rises. I'm curious how much content the final release will have. (Demo)
Deep Among the Swarm is a Strategy Roguelite Tower defense game. Not the best graphics but still they put the assets in a very strategic way where you have to choose which are the best upgrades 8.4
Exciting real time strategy swarm roguelite, endless hours of fun setting up bases and defending them.
A bit like Creeper World. It's fantastic! held my interest for around 40 hours. Eventually the path to the endgame got a bit too samey and repetitive. The rogue-like aspect could be improved though.
